title: Sense of Smell Changes in Parkinson's
content: A reduced or lost sense of smell can occur in some people with Parkinson's disease and may appear before movement symptoms. A person may notice that familiar smells seem weaker or are difficult to detect. Changes in smell can also occur because of aging, respiratory infections, nasal or sinus problems and other medical conditions. A reduced sense of smell alone does not confirm Parkinson's disease and should not be used as a diagnostic test. Persistent or unexplained changes in smell can be discussed with an appropriate healthcare professional.
